title: GPU memory oscillation mitigation and KV policing for mixed-precision continuous batching
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem:

We observe recurrent GPU memory oscillations on 80-series instances when mixed-precision quantized model families and continuous batching are active. Oscillations manifest as repeated KV cache growth/shrink cycles + activation spikes that trigger preemptive evictions and transient QPS drops for high-priority tenants. Root causes appear to be a combination of: uneven KV prefetching on long-tail sequences, suboptimal slab enforcement for weights vs ephemeral activations, and overly-aggressive headroom reclamation during burst windows.

Goal:

Define and implement a GPU memory budgeting and policing layer that: (1) stabilizes memory usage across weights / KV / activations, (2) provides explicit per-tenant headroom reservations and emergency fallback thresholds, (3) supports mixed-precision quantized weights and optional KV compression, and (4) integrates with the continuous-batching pipeline and the autoscaler.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- Measurable reduction in memory oscillation frequency (goal: >= 70% reduction in oscillation-triggered evictions across test fleet).
- No more than a 5% latency p95 regression for P0 routes at target throughput.
- Headroom reservations honored in >= 99.5% of dispatch cycles for non-preemptible tenants under simulated burst load.
- Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback if eviction rate increases by > 10% vs baseline.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Headroom Bands: Introduce three headroom bands per GPU: guaranteed-reserve (weights + pinned KV), soft-reserve (tenant headroom that can be borrowed under explicit policy), and emergency-evict band (last resort for non-critical activations). Each band exposed to scheduler as a numeric quota and an eviction priority.

2) KV Policing: Implement a per-tenant KV policing agent that tracks effective KV delta over sliding window and enforces a max-growth rate. When a tenant’s KV growth violates soft-reserve, agent triggers backpressure signals to batching pipeline (shrink batch size for offending tenant) and optionally applies lightweight on-the-fly KV compression (lossless/low-loss modes).

3) Activation Friction: Add activation friction tokens that slow the acceptance rate of new requests for tenants nearing emergency-evict band. Friction is additive with existing rate limiting and throttle direction is prioritized by route SLA.

4) Memory Accounting Ledger: Extend reserve ledger with epoched reconciliations every 200ms to avoid stale headroom computations; include quantized-weight footprint sampling and compressibility hints from model metadata.

5) Simulation & Test Harness: Expand the existing memory-simulator to include mixed-precision quantization models, synthetic long-tail sequence generators, and KV-compressibility knobs. We'll run multi-tenant scenarios with correlated bursts and step loads.

Tradeoffs & alternatives considered:
- Option A: Aggressive global KV eviction. Simpler but causes user-visible regressions; rejected for P0 tenants.
- Option B: Static per-tenant static caps. Predictable but inefficient for bursty tenants; we prefer soft-reserve + borrow model.
- Option C: Prefer refinement of batcher heuristics alone. Insufficient because weight/activation slab conflicts still cause oscillations.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike (1 week): Prototype KV policing in simulator + pressure signals to batcher.
- PoC (3 weeks): Implement headroom bands and ledger reconciler in runtime; unit tests for eviction priorities.
- Integration (2 weeks): Hook friction tokens to rate limiter and verify canary harness.
- Canary (2 weeks): Deploy to 10 machines in us-west with runtime-2.4 flags; monitor eviction rate/latency.
- Ramp (2–4 weeks): Gradual rollout with auto rollback rules.

Instrumentation and observability:
- New metrics: headroom_used_by_band, kv_growth_rate_per_tenant, eviction_count_by_priority, friction_tokens_in_flight, ledger_reconciliation_latency.
- Dashboards: Grafana panel for oscillation heatmap (per-GPU memory variance over time), canary comparison dashboard, per-tenant KV trend chart.
- Alerts: SLO breach if eviction_count_by_priority for guaranteed-reserve > 0, and if kv_growth_rate_per_tenant > threshold for 30s.

Rollout & safety knobs:
- Feature flag: runtime.memory_policing_v2 (global + per-tenant overrides).
- Canary auto-rollback triggers: >10% eviction increase or >5% p95 latency increase on tracked routes.
- Emergency cutoff: ability to disable per-tenant friction for enterprise tenants with dedicated capacity.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How compressible are production KV caches in aggregate? We need sample histograms from telemetry (requesting a sample job).
- Interaction with existing KV sharding across CPU+GPU: do we need cross-node coordination for headroom enforcement?
- Fine-tuning of friction curve to avoid oscillatory feedback between batcher and friction tokens.

Artifacts / references:
- Simulation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-sim/pull/472 (WIP)
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRV/pages/GPUMemPolicing/Design
- Current canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/oscillation/canary-memory-oscillations

Next steps (this ticket):
- Marcus: finish simulator KV-policing spike and upload synthetic workload traces (ETA 2026-03-12).
- Aisha: land ledger reconciler RFC and add metric hooks in runtime (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Ops: provide KV sample histograms and top-20 tenant compressibility report (requested: ops@redwood, ETA 2026-03-15).

Acceptance criteria for this ticket to be marked Done:
- Simulator demonstrates >=70% reduction in eviction-triggered QPS drops across 5 synthetic scenarios.
- Runtime unit + integration tests for ledger and eviction priorities merged and code-reviewed.
- Canary run completes with metrics meeting success criteria and rollout plan documented.
